lesson (facts): A record the tracker has already rejected can be re-created from fresh articles as a brand new incident: when a new entr
refused: lesson (facts): Never date an attack from a Telegram channel post or a video release: date it from the outlet that reported the strike,
notes: The Aviva is not a new attack: Turkey's Haber Denizde reported the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Aviva, owned by Garanti Denizcilik and managed by Bilka Denizcilik, hit in the Black Sea on 6 October with one seafarer killed and the fire put out, matching the Odesa administration's 6 October report of a Marshall Islands vessel loaded with rapeseed oil hit with one killed and seven injured. Do not lead today's brief with it, do not date it 8 October, and do not say no damage or casualty details were given.

The Strait of Hormuz paragraph mixes three events and must be rebuilt. The Panama flag and the 11 Indian crew injured belong to the 5 October strike on On Peace, already reported. UKMTO's delayed warning of 8 October was a time-late report of a crude oil tanker struck on 6 October with no casualties. The paused escort followed the 8 October attack on the Singapore-flagged Evergreen containership Ever Lovely near Oman, whose crew were safe. Say those two events and drop the Panama tanker and the injured figure.

The 7 October Qatar strike on the Acers, with casualties, is inside the 48 hour window and in the facts but the article never names it: give it one line, credited to UKMTO. The 8 October fire on a tanker off Fujairah, the Marshall Islands-flagged Dhalkut in Euronews reporting, is a separate attack and not part of the Acers incident.
